pages.title: Glass-like ice · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Sunday afternoon at a bright ice rink in Boston. Soft music plays and the ice shines like glass. Families glide in circles with red cheeks and big smiles. Rui stands at the entrance with a scarf and gloves. He has never skated on ice before. A worker named Kim smiles at him.
“Welcome to the rink! Is this your first time?” says Kim. “Yes. I rarely skate. I usually play soccer.” says Rui. “No problem. Do you need rental skates?” says Kim.

pages.title: Glass-like ice · 3/3
paragraphs: “Okay. And what time does the rink close?” says Rui. “At nine. Hot chocolate is at the snack bar.” says Kim. Rui sits on a bench and laces up his rental skates. He steps on the ice and holds the wall. Slowly, he learns to move one foot after the other. After an hour, he skates a full lap alone. He drinks hot chocolate with a proud smile. A new habit can start with one brave step.
